_about: Shelves group the Gurmatveechar series for the Listen pages. Profiles describe the text each series is katha on. Profiles are editorial (AI-assisted, awaiting review). Only well-established facts are stated; where authorship or edition is not known, 'unknown' says so rather than guessing.

shelves.title: Gurbani
shelves.intro: Katha of the Guru's own Word: Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji Ang by Ang, the daily Nitnem banis and individual compositions.

shelves.title: Bhai Gurdas Ji and Bhai Nand Lal Ji
shelves.intro: The writings Sikh tradition reads alongside Gurbani as its closest companions.

shelves.title: Lives of the Gurus and Gurmukhs
shelves.intro: Sacred history told as katha: the great Granths of Kavi Santokh Singh and the lives of mahapurakhs.

shelves.title: Indian philosophy, read through Gurmat
shelves.intro: Katha on classical texts of Vedanta, Yoga, Buddhist and practical wisdom, a long tradition of Sikh learning. The theme pages explain where these texts meet Gurbani and where they differ.

shelves.title: Talks and questions
shelves.intro: Question-and-answer sessions and talks on household life and brahmcharya.

shelves.title: Divans, by place and year
shelves.intro: Recordings of divans in Punjab and with sangats abroad, from 1988 onwards.

sri-guru-granth-sahib-ji-di-lareevar-kat.author: The Sikh Gurus and the Bhagats whose bani the Gurus included
sri-guru-granth-sahib-ji-di-lareevar-kat.about: Babaji's largest body of katha follows Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji Ang by Ang, beginning with the Mool Mantar and Japji Sahib. Most recordings are titled by the Ang range they cover, so any Gurbani line quoted on this site can be traced to the katha of its Ang.

jap-ji-sahib-katha.author: Guru Nanak Dev Ji
jap-ji-sahib-katha.about: The opening bani of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji (Ang 1 to 8): the Mool Mantar, thirty-eight pauris and a closing Salok, recited every morning. Much of Gurmat's vocabulary (Hukam, Naam, nadar, the five khands) is set out here.

nitnem-bani-katha.author: Several: Japji Sahib and Anand Sahib from Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji; Jaap Sahib, Tav Prasad Savaiye and Shabad Hazare Patshahi 10 from Sri Dasam Granth; the Saloks of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
nitnem-bani-katha.about: Katha on the banis of the daily Sikh discipline. The source of each bani is named in the recording titles.

sukhmani-sahib.author: Guru Arjan Dev Ji
sukhmani-sahib.about: ‘The jewel of peace’: twenty-four ashtapadis in Raag Gauri (Ang 262 to 296) on simran, the sadh sangat, the brahmgiani and the Divine. Six recordings.

baramaha.author: Two compositions in the Granth: Guru Arjan Dev Ji (Raag Majh, Ang 133) and Guru Nanak Dev Ji (Raag Tukhari, Ang 1107)
baramaha.about: Songs of the twelve months, in which each season colours the soul's longing for the Beloved. The recording titles do not say which composition each covers.

bhai-gurdas-di-vaaran-di-katha.author: Bhai Gurdas Ji, the scribe of the Adi Granth
bhai-gurdas-di-vaaran-di-katha.about: Forty Punjabi vaars that explain Gurmat and recount the Gurus' lives; Sikh tradition calls them a key to Gurbani. Babaji's katha begins with Bhai Gurdas Ji's own life and continues through Vaar 41.
bhai-gurdas-di-vaaran-di-katha.uncertainty: Scholars generally attribute the forty-first Vaar to a later poet rather than to Bhai Gurdas Ji himself.

bhai-gurdas-de-kabit-savaiye-katha.author: Bhai Gurdas Ji
bhai-gurdas-de-kabit-savaiye-katha.about: Short poems in Braj on the Guru, the Gurmukh and the sangat, traditionally numbered at 675. Fifty-six recordings.

gazlan-bhai-nand-lal-ji.text: Ghazals of Bhai Nand Lal Ji
gazlan-bhai-nand-lal-ji.author: Bhai Nand Lal Ji ‘Goya’, poet at the court of Guru Gobind Singh Ji
gazlan-bhai-nand-lal-ji.about: Persian ghazals of love for the Guru, in the imagery of the Persian mystical tradition. Five recordings.

sri-gurpartap-suraj-parkash-katha.author: Kavi Santokh Singh (completed 1843)
sri-gurpartap-suraj-parkash-katha.about: A vast Braj poem on the lives of the Gurus from Guru Angad Dev Ji to Guru Gobind Singh Ji, arranged in raases and ruts and read in katha across the Panth. Babaji's katha runs to more than a thousand recordings.
sri-gurpartap-suraj-parkash-katha.uncertainty: Historians note that the Granth weaves history, tradition and the outlook of its own time; its episodes are best heard as sacred narrative and weighed against Gurbani.

sri-nanak-parkash-katha.author: Kavi Santokh Singh (1823)
sri-nanak-parkash-katha.about: The life of Guru Nanak Dev Ji in two halves (Purbardh and Utarardh), a forerunner of the Suraj Granth.
sri-nanak-parkash-katha.uncertainty: As with the Suraj Granth, history and tradition are interwoven.

sikh-raaj-ke-usariyo.author: Babaji's katha
sikh-raaj-ke-usariyo.about: The lives of mahapurakhs of the Sikh Raaj era: Baba Sahib Singh Bedi (Una Sahib), Baba Bhag Singh (Kuri), and Baba Bir Singh, Baba Khuda Singh and Baba Maharaj Singh of Naurangabad.

man-budh-atam.author: Babaji
man-budh-atam.about: Nine talks with their subjects in their titles: devotion and love, renouncing the world, the paths of devotion, how wanting obstructs knowledge, the make-up of the mind, devotion and food, who is a yogi, what is the self and what is knowledge.

vedant-darshan.author: ‘Vedanta Darshan’ usually names the Brahma Sutras, traditionally attributed to Badarayana
vedant-darshan.about: The foundational aphorisms of the Vedanta school on the nature of Brahman and the self.
vedant-darshan.uncertainty: The recordings do not say which edition or commentary Babaji read from.

vichar-sagar.author: Nischaldas (19th century)
vichar-sagar.about: A Hindi exposition of Advaita Vedanta, long studied among sadhus and in sant traditions of learning. Twenty-one recordings.

vichar-mala.author: unknown
vichar-mala.about: A short Vedanta text studied alongside Vichar Sagar. Six recordings.

astavakra-gita-katha.author: Traditionally, a dialogue between the sage Ashtavakra and King Janaka
astavakra-gita-katha.about: One of the most uncompromising statements of non-duality: the self is already free and only needs to recognise it. Eleven recordings.

yog-darshan.author: Patanjali
yog-darshan.about: The classical text of Yoga in four chapters, which Babaji's twenty-one recordings follow, beginning with a talk on kundalini shakti.

om-pantanjali-yog-shastar.author: Patanjali
om-pantanjali-yog-shastar.about: Six talks titled Moksh, Naam Di Mehima, Sadhana, Samadhi, Satsangat and Sidhian.

vairaag-shatak.author: The Vairagya Shatakam is attributed to the poet Bhartrihari
vairaag-shatak.about: Verses on the passing nature of pleasure, wealth and youth, and the call to detachment. Thirty-seven recordings across thirteen adhyais.
vairaag-shatak.uncertainty: The thirteen adhyais suggest a version arranged in chapters, perhaps a Punjabi or Braj rendering; the edition is not recorded.

parbodh-chandar-natak-katha.author: After the Sanskrit Prabodha Chandrodaya of Krishna Mishra (11th century)
parbodh-chandar-natak-katha.about: An allegory in which King Discernment (Vivek) battles Great Delusion (Mahamoh) for the soul. Thirty-three recordings.
parbodh-chandar-natak-katha.uncertainty: The title suggests a Punjabi or Braj version; which one is not recorded.

dhampad.author: Verses attributed to the Buddha, from the Pali canon
dhampad.about: A classic anthology of Buddhist verse on the mind, conduct and the ending of craving. Five recordings.

chanaka-raajniti.author: Attributed to Chanakya (Kautilya)
chanaka-raajniti.about: Aphorisms on prudence, friendship, wealth and rule, with two further talks titled Jeevan Jugtan (ways of living).

brahmchari-pati-patni-dharam.author: Babaji
brahmchari-pati-patni-dharam.about: Ten talks on brahmcharya and the duties of husband and wife.

single-divans.author: Babaji
single-divans.about: Individual divans from 1988 onwards, in Punjab and with sangats in the United Kingdom and elsewhere. Many titles give the date and place; some name the shabad or Ang of the katha.

katha-at-gurdwara-ber-sahib-sultanpur-lo.text: Katha at Gurdwara Sri Ber Sahib, Sultanpur Lodhi
katha-at-gurdwara-ber-sahib-sultanpur-lo.author: Babaji
katha-at-gurdwara-ber-sahib-sultanpur-lo.about: Divans at Gurdwara Sri Ber Sahib, including katha on Amavas and on the Gurpurbs of Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Guru Gobind Singh Ji, 2012 and 2013.

guru-nanak-gurdwara-smethwick.author: Babaji
guru-nanak-gurdwara-smethwick.about: Sixteen divans with the sangat at Smethwick, England.

toronto-2009.author: Babaji
toronto-2009.about: Divans at Malton Gurdwara and Nanaksar, Brampton.

australia-2010.author: Babaji
australia-2010.about: Divans at Nanaksar, Blackburn and Sydney.

canada-2010.author: Babaji
canada-2010.about: Gurbani katha during the 2010 visit to Canada.

australia-2011.author: Babaji
australia-2011.about: Divans at Blackburn, Keysborough, Craigieburn, Brisbane, Hobart, Hoppers Crossing and Nanaksar.
